result.summary: The landlord, Miles Kendall, is arranging his own operative, Amelia, to contact the tenant and look at the washing machine and the towel rail (event 011). The tenant has been told this (event 012). The tenant said the drain pump steps didn't fix the machine (event 014), then thanked us for the update (event 015). I passed the failed fix on to the landlord so Amelia knows before she attends, and sent the tenant a short update with a chase date. I also recorded the landlord's contractor arrangement and the machine's history, and put the ticket on a 3-day hold waiting on the landlord.

judgement.why_this_decision: The landlord took the job on himself (event 011). Nothing needs the agency's approval and we have no contractor to assign. The only new information is the tenant saying the drain pump steps didn't work (event 014). That matters for Amelia's diagnosis, so I sent it to the landlord. The tenant had already been told Amelia would call, so they only needed a short update with a date for us to chase. The next step is the landlord's, so I placed a hold with a follow-up date.

alternatives_considered.option: Assign Amelia via assign_contractor and move to scheduling
alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord is instructing Amelia directly. We have no contact details or agency booking for her, and it isn't confirmed that a visit is booked.

alternatives_considered.option: Escalate because the classifier said review
alternatives_considered.why_not: The tenant's 'still broken' is already covered by Amelia's coming visit. There is no safety risk (0.06) and no complaint, so the case doesn't need agency judgement.
Amelia's diagnosis benefits from knowing the pump fix failed, and the tenant had reported it hadn't worked, so a short update with a date was reasonable.
